skill.name: command-management
skill.description: Create or update Claude Code custom slash commands using a structured template and least-privilege tool permissions.
skill.summary: Build consistent Claude Code slash commands with standard frontmatter, scoped tools, and validation steps.
skill.author: Emz1998

security_audit.summary: No prompt injection, network access, credential access, or obfuscated behavior was found. The retained risks are bounded but real: the reference docs describe persistent personal command paths under ~/.claude/commands and Bash interpolation with ! commands. The SKILL.md backtick findings are Markdown formatting false positives for paths and tool names.

remediation.suggestion: Keep default writes restricted to project .claude/commands, and require explicit user confirmation before creating or editing ~/.claude/commands files.
Require explicit approval before adding ! Bash interpolation or Bash allowed-tools, and restrict Bash permissions to exact command allowlists.
Document why each generated command needs its allowed tools, and reject broad filesystem or shell permissions unless the task requires them.

finding_verdicts.reason: The reference documents ! Bash interpolation for git status, so a generated slash command can execute a local command before the prompt runs. The command is hardcoded and read-only, which limits but does not remove the execution risk.

The reference documents ! Bash interpolation for git diff HEAD, which can execute locally and include repository changes in command context. This is intentional Claude Code behavior, but it is still a real local command execution and data exposure surface.

The reference documents ! Bash interpolation for git branch --show-current, causing a local command to run before the slash command body. It is a bounded read-only example, but generated commands using this pattern need explicit Bash permissions.

The reference documents ! Bash interpolation for git log --oneline -10, causing local command execution during slash command use. The example is hardcoded and read-only, but it still expands the command capability surface.

The reference identifies ~/.claude/commands/ as a personal command location, which can persist commands across projects. The skill has a project-only constraint in SKILL.md, so confidence is moderate rather than high.

The reference shows mkdir -p ~/.claude/commands, which creates a hidden user-level command directory. Commands placed there persist beyond the current project, so this is a real filesystem persistence risk if followed.

The reference writes a command file into ~/.claude/commands, creating a user-level slash command. This can affect future projects and sessions, so it is a real persistence risk even though the example is benign.

The reference explains that command descriptions can come from user-level ~/.claude/commands paths. This is documentation rather than an instruction to write, but it still describes a persistent hidden command location.
The reference states that ~/.claude/commands/component.md creates a user-level /component command. This is a real persistent command mechanism that should require explicit user intent before use.

The reference names ~/.claude/commands/ as a command location, which is hidden home-directory access. The project-only constraint in SKILL.md reduces the likelihood that the skill should use it by default.
The reference shows creation of ~/.claude/commands, which is hidden home-directory access. This is legitimate for personal commands but should be gated because it persists outside the repository.
The reference writes a Markdown command file under ~/.claude/commands. That is hidden home-directory file access with persistent effects, even though the sample content is benign.
The reference discusses user-level command directories under ~/.claude/commands. It is descriptive documentation, but it still covers hidden home-directory access patterns.
The reference describes a file at ~/.claude/commands/component.md creating a user command. This is hidden home-directory access that can affect all projects for that user.

content.value_statement: Custom slash commands can become inconsistent, incomplete, or too permissive. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code users through templated command creation with least-privilege permissions.
actual_capabilities: Reads the included slash command documentation before creating commands.
Uses a structured command template with YAML frontmatter and required sections.
Creates or updates command files in the project command directory.
Guides least-privilege allowed-tools choices for each command.
Tests finished commands with the SlashCommand tool when available.
Reports command creation results and validation status.
limitations: Focused on Claude Code style slash commands, not general shell aliases.
Does not guarantee command safety if users request broad tool permissions.
Requires write access to the target command directory.
Testing depends on the SlashCommand tool being available in the host environment.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Command
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for one simple workflow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a project slash command for reviewing pull request changes. Use the standard template and only include tools needed for reading files.

prompt_templates.title: Update an Existing Command
prompt_templates.scenario: Improve a command that already exists.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the existing command for test planning. Update its frontmatter, workflow sections, rules, and acceptance criteria to match the template.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Namespaced Command
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a namespaced project command for frontend component review. Include argument guidance and scoped tool permissions.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Permission-Sensitive Command
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced command requiring careful tool selection.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a release preparation command that may inspect git state. Explain each permission choice and avoid broad shell access unless required.

output_examples.input: Create a command for security review.
output_examples.output: The skill produces a project command with frontmatter, a concise review workflow, least-privilege read permissions, and acceptance criteria.

output_examples.input: Update our planning command to follow the template.
output_examples.output: The skill compares the command to the template, fills missing sections, tightens tool permissions, and reports the validation result.

output_examples.input: Make a frontend component command with arguments.
output_examples.output: The skill creates a namespaced command with an argument hint, component-focused workflow steps, rules, and test instructions.

best_practices: Start with the narrowest allowed tools and add permissions only when the command needs them.
Keep command workflows concise, structured, and focused on repeatable user actions.
Test each command after creation and record any behavior that could not be verified.
anti_patterns: Do not grant broad shell or filesystem permissions for convenience.
Do not place personal commands in a user-level directory without explicit confirmation.
Do not omit frontmatter, argument hints, rules, or acceptance criteria from reusable commands.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates or updates Claude Code custom slash command files using the included command template.

faq.question: Can it edit existing commands?
faq.answer: Yes. It can inspect an existing command and update missing frontmatter, workflow sections, rules, and acceptance criteria.

faq.question: Does it choose command permissions?
faq.answer: It guides permission selection and favors least-privilege allowed tools for the requested workflow.

faq.question: Can it create personal commands?
faq.answer: The skill is constrained to project command paths by default. Personal command changes should require explicit user confirmation.

faq.question: Does it run shell commands?
faq.answer: The skill itself does not require Bash. Generated commands should only include Bash when the user approves a specific need.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
